sentences.text: Ct. 29 vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr on 4 December, 2025

142. Crr 5098 of 2025
04.12.2025
Tuhin Mondal Bd.
 Ct. 29 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & Anr.
 Mr. Kaushik Chatterjee
 Mr. Tirthankar Dey ... for the petitioner.

This is an application wherein petitioner has challenged the impugned proceeding in connection with GR No. 480 of 2024 presently pending before learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class Bidhannagar under sections 420/406/465/468/471/120B of the Indian Penal Code.

Petitioner's contention is that opposite party alleged in the written complaint filed in the form of 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the court below that he availed a balance transfer home loan against property from Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd., who sanctioned a loan amount of Rs.
20,20,000/- on execution of two agreements on the printed form.
The complainant was also provided for personal loan (Top UP Loan) amounting to Rs. 2,30,000/- and Rs. 5,44,140-/.

The complainant was supposed to pay the said amount by three monthly EMI (Equated Monthly Installment) for three loans which the complainant availed from the said financier but the complainant later on discovered that four separate EMI were being deducted from the bank account of the petitioner and upon further enquiry the petitioner detected that the said financier cheated the petitioner by creating false loan account in his name on account of insurance protection amounting to Rs. 1,18,000/- .
Thereafter on multiple occasion complainant raised his concern to the said financier but they did not pay any heed to his request.

Being aggrieved by the aforesaid proceeding learned counsel for the petitioner submits that from the charge-sheet it is clear that the present petitioner Tuhin Mondal, approved the loan on good faith.
However, he has been charge-sheeted only on the basis of the assumption that his liability cannot be ruled out.
In this context petitioner further submits that in an offence under the IPC the concept of vicarious liability is completely unknown.

He further contended that the complainant has not been made an accused in the instant case and as such the proceeding itself is bad in law and must not continue and in support of his contention he has relied upon a judgment of Apex Court in the case of S.C.Garg -vs- State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr., reported in 2025 SCC Online SC 791.

sentences.text: Upon hearing learned counsel for the petitioner, the application is admitted.

Petitioner is directed to serve a copy of the application upon the State through the office of the Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta and upon the opposite party no. 2 through speed post intimating next date of hearing and to file affidavit of service on the returnable date.

sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel for the petitioners prays for stay of the impugned proceeding.

Having heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and that the petitioner has made out an arguable case, which requires adjudication on merit let all further proceedings being GR No.
480 of 2024 presently pending before learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class Bidhannagar, be stayed qua the petitioner only namely Tuhin Mondal, for a period of twelve (12) weeks from date or until further order, whichever is earlier.

Let the matter be listed under the heading "Contested Application" in the monthly list of February,
2026.

(Dr. Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee, J.)
